verdict.root_cause: cartservice's cache dependency (redis-cart) began adding a near-constant ~300ms penalty to every cache operation at around 15:05, and cartservice fails by waiting. Traces show cartservice handler self-time under 1ms while the HGET and HMSET child spans each hold ~300-311ms, reads and writes equally affected, against a pre-onset baseline of 0.2-0.5ms per cache span [tr_a3ca6f1897ee]. The penalty accumulates per call, so AddItem reaches ~605-615ms and a full checkout ~650-660ms end to end, which is what frontend, checkoutservice and loadgenerator noticed at the same minute. The fixed, command-agnostic magnitude matches the 300ms egress delay platform-automation repeatedly injected into cartservice in four apply/revert chaos cycles the same day [tr_7ed48a0748fe], suggesting a further unrecorded injection or an equivalent network-path delay. checkoutservice's spiky 0.4%-mean / 4.1%-peak errors off a flat-zero baseline [tr_81d78e6a5d7b] are downstream fallout: it has no changes of its own [tr_39ea4f72ea51] and logs clean end-to-end orders through 15:07 [tr_358eccc1f9bb].
verdict.reasoning: Traces localise the time precisely: caller-to-callee gaps are 1-2ms, caller self-times 1-3ms, cartservice handler self-time under 1ms, and nearly the whole duration sits in the cache spans [tr_a3ca6f1897ee]. That dispatch also rules out caller-side queueing, cartservice code regression, fan-out, read-path-only explanations and other downstream peers (0-20ms), and finds no error or timeout spans — so the mechanism is waiting, not failing. The onset is real: the same paths were sub-millisecond minutes earlier [tr_a3ca6f1897ee] and checkoutservice steps off an exactly-zero baseline [tr_81d78e6a5d7b]. cartservice is alive and serving densely with no error lines [tr_4160e7d59250], ruling out crash or exhaustion. A flat ~300ms independent of command type and call volume is the signature of an inserted delay rather than organic saturation, and exactly that artifact is documented four times the same day [tr_7ed48a0748fe]. Not bad_config: the failure is the wait on the cache hop, and the wrong-port REDIS_ADDR override is recorded as reverted and would yield connection errors, not clean slow successes. cartservice is blamed over checkoutservice because every caller symptom follows from its outbound cache latency. Confidence is medium because cartservice's own metrics returned no samples in either window — an absence of data, not health [tr_b31c4a72c063].
open_questions: No change record sits at onset; the delay sidecar is logged as removed ~1.6h prior [tr_7ed48a0748fe]. A live pod-spec check for a traffic-shaping container on cartservice would settle whether a fifth, unlogged cycle started.
redis-cart itself was never queried: its latency, memory, eviction and connection metrics would distinguish an injected delay from genuine cache-side degradation.

cartservice has no usable metrics at all [tr_b31c4a72c063], and both log queries truncated away the 15:05 minute itself [tr_4160e7d59250], so the cartservice-to-checkoutservice error link is inferred rather than measured.

alternatives.root_cause: redis-cart is genuinely degraded (saturation, memory pressure or host contention) and the uniform ~300ms is organic rather than injected.
alternatives.why_not: Same failing mechanism and same blamed hop, differing only in why the cache is slow; the flat per-operation constant across both reads and writes [tr_a3ca6f1897ee] fits an inserted delay better than load-dependent saturation, and no redis-side evidence was gathered either way.

alternatives.root_cause: A lingering REDIS_ADDR override pointing cartservice at the wrong port is the failure.
alternatives.why_not: The override is recorded as reverted 1.3h before onset [tr_7ed48a0748fe], and a wrong address would produce connection failures, not uniformly successful 300ms cache calls [tr_a3ca6f1897ee].

proposal.expected_effect: No action. Nothing should change as a result of this proposal: cartservice cache spans (HGET/HMSET) should continue to show ~300-311ms and AddItem ~605-615ms in Tempo, and checkoutservice error ratio should stay in the 0-4% spiky band, until a real cause is confirmed and acted on. The observation that would license an action is a live pod-spec/container inventory for cartservice showing a traffic-shaping container attached, or a redis-cart latency/eviction/connection query showing cache-side degradation; either one converts this from inference to measurement. If the sidecar is found, the correct effect to predict is cache span self-time returning to the pre-onset 0.2-0.5ms baseline within about two minutes of its removal.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if the impairment is in fact a still-attached traffic-shaping sidecar or an active REDIS_ADDR override on cartservice, in which case a revert would have restored sub-millisecond cache spans immediately and I have prolonged a ~650ms checkout for every user. The specific check that would falsify me: a pod-spec inspection of the running cartservice showing a delay/tc container, or a change record dated inside 15:05. But the evidence I have says the opposite - revert_config requires a configuration or flag change named inside the incident window, and [tr_7ed48a0748fe] states all 20 cartservice changes landed before onset, the most recent 1.3h prior, with the delay sidecar logged as removed ~1.6h prior and REDIS_ADDR already reverted to unset. The precondition is not met on the evidence in front of me. Worse, the last recorded 'prior configuration' for cartservice is the chaos state (override image, REDIS_ADDR=redis-cart:6380, delay sidecar), so revert_config could plausibly re-apply the very fault being diagnosed. rollback_image is ruled out by the same record (no deploy in the window, last image revert ~1.9h prior). restart_service requires evidence pointing at process state; [tr_a3ca6f1897ee] puts the time in the downstream cache hop with sub-1ms cartservice handler self-time, and logs show the process serving normally through 15:07, so process state is not implicated - and a restart is irreversible. scale_service is unavailable. Nothing permitted targets redis-cart or the network path, which is where the mechanism lives, and redis-cart is not in the blast radius.
proposal.risk: The risk of the abstention is continued impact: frontend and checkoutservice users keep seeing ~605-660ms cart and checkout operations and checkoutservice keeps spiking to ~4% errors for as long as this goes unremediated. The risk being avoided is larger: a revert_config on cartservice that re-applies the chaos-cycle configuration would move cartservice's Redis address to a non-default port or re-attach the 300ms delay, turning a pure-latency incident into a hard cart failure, and would do so via an action the brief calls reversible only in the sense that the config can be swapped back - the container recreate and lost cache are not undone. A restart would discard cart cache state irreversibly while leaving a network-path delay untouched.
proposal.blast_radius: No services change state. Had an action been taken on cartservice, its inbound callers frontend and checkoutservice would see connection resets during the recreate, loadgenerator would register the resulting errors, and checkoutservice's downstream order flow (payment, email, queue) would show gaps in the offsets currently running clean per [tr_358eccc1f9bb]. Note also that cartservice has no usable error-ratio or restart metrics at all [tr_b31c4a72c063] and its logs truncated away the onset minute, so the effect of any action on cartservice could only be confirmed through Tempo spans and its callers' metrics - a poor position from which to act blind.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Four services alerting simultaneously along the cart/checkout/frontend path is a coordinated failure, not a single quiet warning, so it cannot be dismissed. The synchronous onset across a shared call chain weakly suggests a common downstream dependency, but nothing rests on that guess.
